name: Urijah
overview: Urijah was a male Levite priest notable for constructing an altar following the design seen in Damascus, demonstrating a connection to broader ancient Near Eastern religious practices. He is also recognized as one of the faithful witnesses mentioned in Isaiah 8:2, highlighting his role in upholding true worship during a challenging period for Israel. His priestly service places him within the tribe of Levi, dedicated to the service of God.
namesAndTitles: The name Urijah, also rendered Uriah, means 'YHWH is [my] flame, light,' reflecting a profound recognition of God's illuminating and purifying presence. This meaning underscores the spiritual role associated with his priestly office and his faithfulness as a witness. Both name forms appear in Scripture, emphasizing the same divine attribute.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Urijah beyond his identity as a Levite priest and his role described in the unique attributes. There are no additional familial connections documented in the biblical text concerning him.
scriptureSignificance: Urijah's significance lies in his faithful priestly witness and his involvement in the construction of an altar patterned after that in Damascus, which indicates a period of religious and political interaction influencing Israelite worship. His mention as a faithful witness in Isaiah 8:2 further affirms his commitment to God's truth amidst a time of national crisis. Together, these elements portray Urijah as a figure who maintained the worship of the true God and served as a spiritual example during a turbulent era.
